title: Replica Lag Assumes Sync Read
readme_md:
# Replica Lag Assumes Sync Read

**Category:** Debugging  
**Difficulty:** Medium  

## Scenario

The internal admin panel shows stale profile fields for minutes after a successful save. The save toast says “updated,” refresh sometimes shows the old email, then later it flips. Support thinks it is caching in the browser, but repro happens with cache disabled.

The read path was written when you only had one database. You added a replica for scale and kept the old call shape.

## Background

Writes go to the primary. Reads for this screen are supposed to honor a consistency hint after edits so operators do not file duplicate tickets. Analytics traffic still prefers the replica for cost.

## System Context

- The workflow crosses service boundaries where retries, duplicate delivery, and partial failure are normal.
- Operators rely on logs/metrics/audit events to replay incidents and verify recovery.
- Downstream consumers depend on stable response envelopes and event semantics.

## Constraints

- Do not rename `get_display_field` or `apply_profile_update` used by tests.
- Returned values stay plain strings or `None` as tests expect.
- The replica may legitimately lag; the bug is in how this code path chooses where to read.

## Your Task

- Fix the read-after-write behavior so consistent reads reflect recent updates.
- Keep replica usage where it still makes sense for tests that expect stale replica reads without the consistency hint.

import pytest

from admin_api import catch_up_replica, save_email_and_render, seed_demo_user
from profiles import apply_profile_update, get_display_field, reset_profile_stores


@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
def _clean():
    reset_profile_stores()
    yield
    reset_profile_stores()


def test_post_write_panel_reads_new_email_when_consistent():
    seed_demo_user("u1", "old@example.com", "Ada")
    apply_profile_update("u1", email="new@example.com")
    assert get_display_field("u1", "email", read_consistent=True) == "new@example.com"


def test_plain_replica_read_without_hint_can_stay_stale():
    seed_demo_user("u2", "a@example.com", "Bob")
    apply_profile_update("u2", email="b@example.com")
    assert get_display_field("u2", "email", read_consistent=False) == "a@example.com"


def test_after_replication_replica_matches_primary():
    seed_demo_user("u3", "x@example.com", "Cid")
    apply_profile_update("u3", email="y@example.com")
    catch_up_replica("u3")
    assert get_display_field("u3", "email", read_consistent=False) == "y@example.com"


def test_new_user_create_then_consistent_read():
    seed_demo_user("u4", "seed@example.com", "Dee")
    apply_profile_update("u4", email="first@example.com")
    assert get_display_field("u4", "email", read_consistent=True) == "first@example.com"


def test_two_writes_latest_value_on_consistent_read():
    seed_demo_user("u5", "v0@example.com", "Eve")
    apply_profile_update("u5", email="v1@example.com")
    apply_profile_update("u5", email="v2@example.com")
    assert get_display_field("u5", "email", read_consistent=True) == "v2@example.com"


def test_other_user_unchanged_when_updating_peer():
    seed_demo_user("left", "L@example.com", "L")
    seed_demo_user("right", "R@example.com", "R")
    apply_profile_update("left", email="L2@example.com")
    assert get_display_field("right", "email", read_consistent=False) == "R@example.com"


def test_display_name_field_consistent_read():
    seed_demo_user("u6", "m@example.com", "OldName")
    apply_profile_update("u6", display_name="NewName")
    assert get_display_field("u6", "display_name", read_consistent=True) == "NewName"


def test_save_email_and_render_integration():
    seed_demo_user("u7", "z@example.com", "Zed")
    panel = save_email_and_render("u7", "z2@example.com", read_consistent=True)
    assert panel == "z2@example.com"


def test_missing_user_returns_none():
    assert get_display_field("ghost", "email", read_consistent=True) is None


def test_consistent_hint_does_not_break_replica_only_analytics_path():
    seed_demo_user("u8", "p@example.com", "Pat")
    assert get_display_field("u8", "email", read_consistent=False) == "p@example.com"

# soul.md prebake · #42 Replica Lag Assumes Sync Read

## What this problem really tests

**Consistency model literacy**: distributed databases offer multiple consistency guarantees with different trade-offs. Knowing which guarantee a specific call site needs — and which the codebase actually provides — is foundational. Different callers in the same module can legitimately want different guarantees.

You're also tested on **distinguishing feature from bug**: when a replica returns stale data, that may be a deliberate design choice (cost savings, throughput) rather than a defect. The bug is often in how the code chooses to use the replica, not in the replica itself.

And on **using existing hints as routing keys**: when a function already accepts a boolean kwarg that names the consistency requirement, the implementation must honor it. Ignoring the kwarg makes it dead-code documentation that misleads callers.

## Good prompts to give your AI

- "What kwargs or parameters does this function already accept that suggest different code paths? Are they actually used in the body?"
- "Which industry consistency model does this hint represent — read-your-writes, monotonic reads, eventual consistency, strong consistency?"
- "Are there separate caller use cases that legitimately want different consistency guarantees? Map each caller to the model it needs."
- "What's the difference between 'replica lag is a bug' and 'replica lag is a deliberate trade-off'? Which one describes this codebase?"
- "If a kwarg is documented in the function's docstring but ignored in the body, what does that signal?"

## Reflexes to fight

- **Forcing synchronous replication on every write** — that defeats the whole point of replicas (throughput, cost) and breaks the analytics path
- **Always reading from primary** — that satisfies the consistent test but breaks the analytics test that explicitly expects stale data
- **Adding a cache invalidation layer** — wrong problem; this isn't a cache issue
- **Wrapping reads in a distributed lock** — way too heavy; the existing kwarg is exactly the right hint
- **Changing the function signature or return type** — public API observed by callers; preserved by the problem constraints
- **"Fixing" the docstring to match the buggy code** — the docstring documents the intent; the code is what's wrong

## Design patterns / concepts this problem maps to

- **Read-your-writes consistency** (Wikipedia "Consistency model") — a process that performs a write sees its own write on subsequent reads
- **Eventual consistency** (Wikipedia) — without new updates, all replicas converge to the same value; lag is part of the model
- **Replica lag** (AWS RDS docs) — monitored metric, not eliminated; trade-off for throughput
- **Per-request consistency hints** — let callers declare their requirement instead of forcing a one-size-fits-all model
- **Primary/replica routing** — common database scaling pattern; route by caller's consistency need
- **Hint kwarg as routing key** — the boolean kwarg encodes the routing decision; honoring it is the implementation

## When to ask tips-agent for help

| Situation | What to ask |
|---|---|
| Considering synchronous writes to both | "Does that break the path that deliberately expects stale data?" |
| Considering always-primary reads | "Same — does any test rely on the replica being read for non-consistent callers?" |
| Looking at the function's kwargs | "Is there already a hint that names the consistency requirement? Is it being honored?" |
| Unsure which consistency model the hint represents | "Compare the kwarg's docstring to read-your-writes, monotonic reads, eventual. Which one matches?" |
| Tempted to add caching | "Is the symptom a cache issue or a routing issue? Where does data actually come from?" |

## Reading the failing test as the source of truth

When two tests exist — one expecting fresh data with a consistency flag set, another expecting stale data with the flag unset — the implementation must produce different behavior for each flag value. A function that ignores the flag fails one test or the other; honoring the flag passes both.

## Self-check before submitting

- Did your fix make the consistent-read path use the primary?
- Did your fix preserve the replica-read path for the analytics use case?
- Did you preserve the entry function's signature and return type?
- Did you avoid touching the write path (writes are already correct)?
- Did you add a regression test verifying both consistency paths independently?
- For teaching variant: did you cite a consistency-model reference (Wikipedia, AWS docs) to anchor your routing decision?
